chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from al-Husayn ibn Abu Hamzah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: My father (peace be upon him) said:

Verily, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hanafiyyah was a calm man (with a gesture of his hand). While he was performing the circumambulation of the Ka'bah, al-Hajjaj approached him and said: 'I am inclined to strike the one who has your eyes.' Muhammad replied to him: 'No, verily, for Allah, Blessed is His Name, in His creation are three hundred moments or glances every day. Perhaps one of them may suffice you instead of me.'
ai.seo_question: What is the story of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah and al-Hajjaj in al-Tawhid?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* illustrates the concept of divine omnipotence (Qudrah) through the calm demeanor of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah during his encounter with the formidable Umayyad governor al-Hajjaj. The reference to 'three hundred moments' (or glances) underscores the Shia scholarly view that God’s power is not static but actively and continuously engaged with creation, offering a theological basis for patience and trust in divine timing amidst political turmoil.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 7. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab, on the authority of Ja`far ibn Bashir, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Abu Hamzah that I hear Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) say: My father (AS) say: My father (AS) said: “

Verily, Muhammad ibn `Ali ibn al-Hanafiyyah was a calm man. While he was performing the circumambulation of the Ka`bah – pointing with his hand – al-Hajjaj approached him and said: “I am interested in killing someone who has your eyes.” Muhammad replied to him, “Nay! Verily, for Allah, Blessed be His name, are 300 moments everyday in His Creation. Then probably one of them may suffice you instead of me (implying the moment of death may come to you any time).”
